We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps forward are:
1) Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling) -> retrosynthesis: break amide to carboxylic acid + amine.
2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the side chain). So retrosynthesis: break the C=C and carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. So retrosynthetic step: disconnect the double bond and carboxyl to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid (or its derivative). So we need to identify the fragment: the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is after amide formation? Wait the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... The amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain. The Doebner modification yields an alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the acid). Then later coupling forms amide with an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give acid (alpha,beta-unsaturated) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break unsaturated acid to aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline to give sulfonamide. So we need sulfonyl chloride precursor: NS(=O)(=O)Cl attached to aromatic ring. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the same aniline? Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first aromatic ring (toluene). So we need to disconnect N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the same aromatic amine). So overall three steps: 1) amide formation (coupling) -> precursors: unsaturated acid (aryl acrylic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) Doebner modification -> precursors: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). 3) sulfonamide formation -> precursors: sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the toluene ring with NH2). Wait the aniline used in step 1 is the aniline attached to the unsaturated acid (Nc3ccccc3N). That's a diamine? Actually the amide is C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl ring that also has an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring that also has an NH2 (para?). The SMILES: ...C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 (an aniline). So the amide precursor is the aniline (para-aminophenyl) as nucleophile, and the unsaturated acid as electrophile. So step 1: amide coupling between unsaturated acid and 4-aminophenyl (or 2-? Actually the phenyl with NH2). So we need to propose that.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation from acid and amine? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'

This appears to be reverse of amide formation: product is amide with conjugated double bond; reactants are t-butyl ester? Actually left side is amide, right side is t-butyl ester + acid? Not sure. But we can use it as amide formation template.

We also need a Doebner modification template. Search for functional groups broken: aldehyde, formed: C-C double bonds, carboxylic acid. Let's search again with correct functional groups: broken aldehydes, formed C-C double bonds and aliphatic carboxylic acid? The Doebner forms unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So broken: aldehydes, carboxylic esters? Actually malonic acid provides carboxylic acid groups, but they become one carboxylic acid after decarboxylation. So broken: aldehydes, carboxylic esters? Not sure. Let's search for templates with functional_groups_broken ["aldehydes"] and functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds", "aliphatic carboxylic acid"].
